rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a configuration that combines advanced components (scgpt RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) to evaluate their potential impact on performance. This tests critical design choices (advanced encoders, complex aggregation, effective fusion) that are likely to influence results significantly, providing early insights into which components matter most.

The existing evidence shows that using scgpt RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and weighted fusion achieves 0.52 validation accuracy. This experiment tests avgpool aggregation (vs transformer in config_051) with the same RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion. It clarifies whether aggregation method significantly impacts performance, a critical design choice with sparse evidence yet high uncertainty.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scgpt and imagenet_vit_l encoders (config_049) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.542). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (used in config_051 but with lower accuracy) and fusion from weighted to concat (a simpler method) could improve performance. It clarifies the relative importance of aggregation methods and fusion strategies, which are critical design choices with sparse evidence in the current history.

Existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation with weighted fusion (config_049) achieves higher accuracy (0.542) than transformer aggregation with concat fusion (config_050). This experiment tests whether using avgpool aggregation with concat fusion (config_048) could yield similar performance, clarifying the importance of fusion type. It directly addresses a key design choice (fusion method) with minimal changes to the proven high-performing base (avgpool aggregation).

Existing evidence shows config_049 (avgpool+weighted) has the highest accuracy. This experiment tests transformer aggregation with concat fusion, which could clarify whether aggregation method (avgpool vs transformer) and fusion type (concat vs weighted) matter. It's a logical extension of the current best configuration and addresses uncertainty about these key design choices.

Existing evidence shows that single-modal models with pca_n2000 and transformer aggregation (config_026) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether multimodal configurations with pca_n2000 and transformer aggregation, combined with weighted fusion, can surpass this baseline. It clarifies the impact of fusion methods and aggregation choices in multimodal settings, which are critical for improving performance while balancing exploration of key design decisions.

Existing evidence shows that pca_n2000 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion achieves high accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (a different architecture) maintains performance, clarifying the importance of image encoder choice. It directly extends the promising direction of pca_n2000 RNA and transformer aggregation while exploring a key design decision with potential impact.

Existing evidence shows that pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder combinations (config_026, 020, 028) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests transformer aggregation with weighted fusion for the same RNA/image encoder pair, which could clarify if aggregation method improvements can further enhance performance. It's a logical extension of the current top-performing setup (config_026) and addresses uncertainty about aggregation method impact.

Existing evidence shows pca_n2000 with resnet50 and transformer aggregation (config_026) achieves high accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests scgpt with resnet50 and transformer aggregation (config_044), which could clarify whether the RNA encoder (scgpt vs pca_n2000) significantly impacts performance when paired with resnet50. This balances exploitation of the resnet50+transformer combination with exploration of the scgpt encoder, a key design decision with potential for higher performance.

Existing evidence shows that pca_n2000 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder and transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA encoder with resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion, clarifying whether RNA encoder choice (pca_n2000 vs scvi_n200) impacts performance when using the same image encoder and aggregation method. It balances exploitation of strong image encoder/agg combo with exploration of RNA encoder variations.
